entities.summary: Walter Philip Reuther was an American leader of organized labor and civil rights activist who built the United Automobile Workers (UAW) into one of the most progressive labor unions in American history. He considered labor movements not as narrow special interest groups but as instruments to advance social justice and human rights in democratic societies. He leveraged the UAW's resources and influence to advocate for workers' rights, civil rights, women's rights, universal health care, public education, affordable housing, environmental stewardship, profit-sharing for employees, and nuclear nonproliferation around the world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Walter Reuther's leadership in the United Automobile Workers (UAW) helped establish a model for progressive labor unions that influenced civil rights and social justice movements globally. His advocacy contributed to landmark legislation, such as the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, which improved working conditions and worker protections.
